title: Preregistered tests of equal-resource spectra in aquatic size data
status: Specified and committed BEFORE any of these analyses were computed. The git history of this file is the preregistration record.
rationale: Every positive signal obtained so far is exploratory: a post hoc subrange of a re-expression of a single model-assisted reconstruction. These tests fix the domain, the resource, the exponent mapping and the tolerance in advance.

blinding.test_A: BLIND. Only the categorical design columns of GLOSSAQUA_Size.txt were inspected (method, axis type, units). No Slope value has been read.
blinding.test_B: PARTIALLY BLIND. Point estimates of the top-200m spectrum were already seen; the published uncertainties were not used before.
blinding.test_C: BLIND. The full-water-column table has not been inspected.

test_A_glossaqua.question: Across independently published aquatic size spectra, are the reported slopes equivalent to the value implied by equal biomass per logarithmic size class?
test_A_glossaqua.source: Ersoy et al. 2025, GLOSSAQUA, github.com/zeynepersoy/GLOSSAQUA_dataset, data/GLOSSAQUA_Size.txt
test_A_glossaqua.independence: Different authors, ecosystems, instruments and methods from the Hatton et al. ocean reconstruction. Not derived from it.
inclusion: XaxisParameterType == 'body mass' (mass is the resource; length/volume would need a species-specific conversion exponent that is not available)
Slope, SizeRangeMinimum and SizeRangeMaximum all finite
SizeSpectrumMethod in the mapping table below

exponent_mapping._derivation: With resource q = body mass m, orthopolity is dR/dln m = mean_q * dN/dln m = constant.

Normalized biomass spectrum (linear).why: NBSS b(m) ~ m^s is biomass per unit mass; biomass per log class is m*b(m) ~ m^(1+s); flat requires s = -1

Normalized abundance spectrum (linear).why: normalized abundance a(m) ~ m^s; biomass per log class ~ m^(2+s); flat requires s = -2

Maximum Likelihood.why: MLE of the individual size distribution p(m) ~ m^b; biomass per log class ~ m^(b+2); flat requires b = -2

excluded_methods.Abundance spectrum (linear): binning convention (linear vs logarithmic bin width) not recorded, so the exponent cannot be mapped reliably

test_A_glossaqua.statistic: departure s = reported_slope - predicted_slope. s = 0 is exact orthopolity.
test_A_glossaqua.tolerance: Per study, |s| <= ln(F)/ln(SizeRangeMaximum/SizeRangeMinimum), the slope implying at most an F-fold systematic drift across that study's own reported size range. F = 1.25 primary, F = 2.0 secondary.
test_A_glossaqua.uncertainty: Percentile bootstrap over StudyID blocks, 2000 replicates, seed 20260909. Studies contribute many spectra and are not independent within themselves.
outcomes: fraction_equivalent: fraction of spectra with |s| <= its own tolerance
pooled median s with block-bootstrap interval
median implied drift factor across each study's reported range

declared_success_criteria.supported: pooled median s interval lies entirely inside the median tolerance band AND fraction_equivalent at F=2 >= 0.50
declared_success_criteria.partially_supported: exactly one of those two holds

test_B_ocean_uncertainty.question: Given the published reconstruction uncertainties, can the ocean spectrum be given an equivalence verdict, and are the boundary departures larger than the uncertainty?
test_B_ocean_uncertainty.source: Hatton et al. 2021, summary_biomass_top200_table_long.csv, with the published per-group 95% intervals
test_B_ocean_uncertainty.uncertainty_model: The published interval is exactly [estimate/f, estimate*f] with f the per-group factor in group_standard_errors.csv (verified for all 253 rows). Draw ln(biomass) ~ Normal(ln(estimate), ln(f)/1.96) independently per group per bin, sum groups within a bin, 20000 draws, seed 20260909.
test_B_ocean_uncertainty.model_caveat: This propagates the authors' reported reconstruction uncertainty. It is NOT a resampling of independent observations, and independence across groups and bins is an assumption that will overstate precision if errors are correlated.
outcomes: slope interval and equivalence verdict for the full 23-bin range
same for the post hoc plateau (still exploratory, reported as such)
for each bin, whether the 95% interval of ln(Phi) excludes the declared tolerance band -- i.e. whether that bin's departure is resolvable at all

test_C_full_water_column.question: Does the plateau appear in the full water column, not only the upper 200 m?
test_C_full_water_column.source: Hatton et al. 2021, summary_biomass_table_long.csv (not previously inspected)
test_C_full_water_column.independence: A different observational domain, but the same authors, methods and reconstruction. NOT an independent replication; reported as a second domain.
test_C_full_water_column.procedure: Identical pipeline to test B, including the same plateau boundaries, applied without further tuning.

common.criteria: Flatness requires BOTH slope equivalence (TOST) and bounded departure max|ln Phi| within tolerance.
common.no_reselection: No domain, subset, method mapping or tolerance may be changed after results are seen. Any change creates a new hypothesis and the original stays in the record.
